_comment: Every measured result this project is willing to put in the README.
One rule: a row may only exist here if a COMMITTED file carries its
numbers and a test pins that file. `source` names the file, `pinned_by`
names the test. scripts/make_results_chart.py renders this into the two
SVGs in this directory, and tests/test_results_chart.py fails if a row
and its source ever disagree, or if the committed SVGs go stale.
`lift_points` is the per-QUESTION lift wherever the source records one.
Answering a question three times gives three answers, not three
independent facts, so the per-answer figure has a larger denominator and
a narrower interval. A line that mixes the two levels states a figure
that is comparable to neither, so every row here carries one `level`.
`show_in_readme` decides what the chart draws. A row set false is still
verified by tests/test_results_chart.py and still lives here -- the
finding is kept and checked. The BI comparison is shown beside the
Two rows added 2026-09-13 are ARM-AGAINST-ARM, not context-against-none,
so read their direction from the label and not from the sign. Both are
hidden because they compare two context variants rather than context against none.

results.label: a BI model with no written descriptions
oracle selection against sending every sentence
results.direction_note: without = every sentence (the blob), with = this question's own sentence. A negative lift means the blob won.

results.label: repairing quoted values against the real column values
results.direction_note: without = the sentence as written, with = every quoted literal repaired. A positive lift means the repair helped.
